Runs <command> with the project's secrets (plus "shared") as environment variables.
import opens a .env (default: ./.env) in Fidelius's Import preview for the project (default:
this folder's name); nothing is saved until you click Import there.
export opens Fidelius to write the project's keys to a .env (default: ./.env); you approve it
there. --example writes a .env.example with names only, right away. Most tools don't need a
.env: run them with accio <project> <command>. A .env is for tools that only read a file
(docker compose env_file), apps started from a GUI, or pasting into a dashboard.
Secrets are managed in the Fidelius app. When an AI agent runs accio (or FIDELIUS_MASK=1
is set), secret values in the command's output are masked; --no-mask turns that off.

content.text:
`npm run sync` fails because `PAYMENTS_API_URL` isn't set anywhere. `src/sync.js` silently fell back to `http://127.0.0.1:9`, so the request got `ECONNREFUSED`. `PAYMENTS_KEY` is set. The `shared` secrets only hold `DATABASE_URL`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `PAYMENTS_KEY` and `WEATHER_API_KEY`.

I changed `src/sync.js` to remove the localhost fallback and exit with a clear message if either variable is missing. It also now prints `err.message` instead of the full axios error dump. Running it now prints `sync failed: missing env var(s): PAYMENTS_API_URL`. I haven't confirmed a real sync, because I don't know your payments endpoint.

To finish the fix, add `PAYMENTS_API_URL` to the `shared` project in the Fidelius app, set to your payments provider's base URL. Then re-run `npm run sync`. I didn't set it myself because I'd be guessing the URL.
